drafts.type: asked by name vs who's best
drafts.text:
Ask ChatGPT about a local business by name and its site gets cited 77.6% of the time. Ask "who's the best electrician in town" and it's 2.2%. (study via @alexgroberman)

The second question is where new customers come from. That's the one to build for.
keywords: asked by name vs 'who is best'
drafts.video_tip: Video tip (@BourgAnthony, about 15 sec, vertical screen recording): in ChatGPT, ask 'who's the best [trade] in [city]?' and then ask about [business name] by name. Show both answers back to back. Caption: 'Same business. Two different questions.' Only use what the answers really say; if the business shows up in both, say so.
drafts.best_time_ct: Weekday late morning CT; the standing 8:54 AM slot works for one a day.

drafts.text:
Microsoft now shows businesses how to get traffic from AI search right inside Bing Webmaster Tools. (h/t @alexgroberman)

Plenty of local businesses never set Bing up at all. It's free and takes a few minutes.

If you only did Google, do Bing this week.
keywords: Bing / Microsoft webmaster tools AI traffic

drafts.text:
Page one of Google used to be enough. Now, as @CyrusShepard put it, if you rank top 10 but don't show up in the AI answer, you're practically invisible.

The fix is mostly the old basics: a clear services page, your real address, and the towns you cover.
